social.title: Afternoon Wine at Brix & Mortar in Yaletown
social.description: Tucked into a converted 1912 warehouse with a courtyard garden, Brix runs one of Vancouver's strongest wine programs in a room that actually rewards slowing down.
social.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair something unexpected with whatever you're eating — no vetoing the choice.

social.title: Catch a Show at the Rickshaw Theatre
social.description: The Rickshaw is Vancouver's most lovably unpolished venue — a rescued 1971 movie palace on East Hastings where punk, hip-hop, and indie bills hit harder for the room they're in.
social.bonus: Stand front and centre for at least three songs.

social.title: Saturday Night at The Fox Cabaret on Main
social.description: A former adult cinema turned the most charismatic small music venue on Main Street, The Fox books the kind of eclectic acts that locals actually argue about the next morning.
social.bonus: Get to the front of the crowd before the headliner starts and stay there for the full set.

social.title: Afternoon Pint at The Alibi Room in Gastown
social.description: Vancouver's original craft beer bar has been anchoring Gastown since 2006 with one of the best rotating tap lists in Western Canada — sit at the bar and let the bartender pick.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender for their most unexpected beer recommendation and commit to a full pint.

social.title: Late Night Dumplings at Peaceful Restaurant on Kingsway
social.description: This no-frills Kingsway institution has been serving hand-folded Northern Chinese dumplings until past midnight for decades, and they taste better after 11pm.
social.bonus: Order one dish you can't pronounce and eat it without asking what's in it.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at The Narrow Lounge
social.description: Mount Pleasant's most charming dive bar is genuinely narrow — one long room, cheap drinks, pinball, and a jukebox that somehow always plays the right song.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to a game of pinball — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Evening at Fortune Sound Club in Chinatown
social.description: Vancouver's best dance room hides behind a nondescript Chinatown door with a sound system that makes the floor move and a booking policy that brings legitimate international DJs.
social.bonus: Dance to a genre you would never normally choose — no leaving the floor for the first 30 minutes.

social.title: Trivia Night at The Bimini Pub in Kitsilano
social.description: Kits' oldest dive bar runs a punishing Wednesday trivia night where neighbourhood regulars take absolutely no prisoners and the beer is still priced from another era.
social.bonus: Join a table of strangers instead of forming your own team — introduce yourself with a fake occupation.

social.title: Live Jazz at the Guilt & Co. Underground
social.description: Duck below Gastown street level into this stone-walled basement venue where serious jazz musicians play to a crowd that actually listens.
social.bonus: Buy a drink for the musician nearest you after the set and ask them what they're working on.

social.title: A Pint at The Irish Heather Shebeen
social.description: After 24 years in Gastown the Heather decamped to Chinatown — the long-table gastropub and its whisky shebeen live on at East Georgia.
social.bonus: Captain the team and place the final bet on a category you know nothing about.

social.title: Craft Brewery Hop in Mount Pleasant
social.description: Walk the Mount Pleasant brewery district and sample your way through Vancouver's tightest cluster of taprooms.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender to pick your next pour, no menu.

social.title: Interactive Exhibits at Science World
social.description: Play your way through hands-on exhibits under the giant silver geodesic dome on False Creek.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to the reaction-time game.

chill.title: Morning Tai Chi in Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
chill.description: The only authentic Suzhou-style scholar's garden outside China has been holding the city's attention since 1986, and early morning here before the crowds arrive is genuinely still.
chill.bonus: Sit beside the central pond for 20 minutes without looking at your phone.

chill.title: Saturday Morning at Trout Lake Farmers Market
chill.description: The East Van Community Centre market at Trout Lake is the most neighbourhood-authentic farmers market in the city — mostly vendors you can actually talk to, zero corporate booths.
chill.bonus: Buy one ingredient you've never cooked with and ask the vendor exactly how to use it.

chill.title: Wander the Bloedel Conservatory
chill.description: Inside this domed triodetic geodesic on top of QE Park, over 500 exotic birds fly free among tropical plants while Vancouver rain hammers the glass above you — it's absurdly peaceful.
chill.bonus: Get a free-roaming parrot to land on your arm — stand still and patient until it happens.

chill.title: Browse Macleod's Books on West Pender
chill.description: One of Canada's great independent used bookshops packs floor-to-ceiling stacks into a cramped downtown space that has been a literary refuge since 1974.
chill.bonus: Buy a book whose cover you like but whose plot you know nothing about — read the first page before you leave the store.

chill.title: Sunset at Prospect Point in Stanley Park
chill.description: Watch the freighters queue under the Lions Gate Bridge at golden hour from the highest point in Stanley Park — it's the view that makes locals stop complaining about rent.
chill.bonus: Stay until the very last sliver of sun disappears behind Vancouver Island — not one minute before.

chill.title: Sunset at Kitsilano Beach
chill.description: Watch the sun drop behind the North Shore mountains from Vancouver's most laid-back beach.
chill.bonus: Stay until the mountains turn pink — no photos until then.

chill.title: Picnic at Queen Elizabeth Park
chill.description: Claim a patch of grass at the city's highest point and take in the skyline, mountains, and quarry gardens.
chill.bonus: Bring a snack you've never packed for a picnic before.

chill.title: Stroll VanDusen Botanical Garden
chill.description: Wander 55 acres of themed gardens, a floating boardwalk, and a giant hedge maze in the middle of the city.
chill.bonus: Find the hedge maze and actually solve it.

chill.title: Visit Dude Chilling Park
chill.description: Track down Vancouver's unofficially-officially renamed park and its infamous reclining statue.
chill.bonus: Recreate the statue's pose for a photo.

adventure.title: Sunrise Hike to Black Mountain Lookout in Cypress
adventure.description: Leave the trailhead before dawn and you'll hit the Black Mountain summit platform just as the sun clears the North Shore peaks and lights up the city below.
adventure.bonus: Make coffee on a small stove at the summit and don't move until you've finished the cup.

adventure.title: Skate the Plaza at Hastings Park
adventure.description: Vancouver's best free outdoor skate plaza sits inside Hastings Park and runs legitimate street-style lines that attract serious skaters daily.
adventure.bonus: Land a trick on the manual pad that you've been avoiding — film it.

adventure.title: Volleyball at Sunset Beach Courts
adventure.description: The drop-in beach volleyball scene at Sunset Beach draws a serious crowd all summer and welcomes strangers who can hold their own.
adventure.bonus: Join a game with people you've never met and stay until your team loses.

adventure.title: Trail Run the Baden-Powell from Deep Cove to Mount Seymour
adventure.description: This punishing North Shore segment climbs through old-growth fir and rewards you with ridge views that justify every burning step.
adventure.bonus: Run the entire descent without walking — no stops, no excuses.

adventure.title: Morning Swim at Second Beach Pool
adventure.description: Stanley Park's saltwater outdoor pool is the most civilized way to start a Vancouver morning, with the ocean just beyond the railing.
adventure.bonus: Swim the full length without stopping, then do it again in reverse before getting out.

adventure.title: Bouldering at The Hive Climbing Gym on Grandview
adventure.description: East Van's flagship bouldering gym has routes set aggressively enough to humble experienced climbers and a community vibe that makes first-timers feel welcome within minutes.
adventure.bonus: Pick the hardest problem in the room and attempt it at least five times before moving on — no skipping.

adventure.title: Run the Seawall from Olympic Village to Granville Island
adventure.description: This flat False Creek loop past houseboats, herons, and the Burrard Bridge is the city's best urban run — short enough to be casual, scenic enough to feel like a reward.
adventure.bonus: Run the whole thing without earbuds — stay aware of every sound the city makes.

adventure.title: Swim Canada's Longest Pool at Kitsilano
adventure.description: At 137 metres, Kits Pool is the longest outdoor saltwater pool in Canada and lapping it at high tide with the mountains straight ahead is a genuinely absurd privilege.
adventure.bonus: Swim the full length non-stop ten times — no touching the wall between laps.

adventure.title: Hike to Quarry Rock in Deep Cove
adventure.description: The hike to Quarry Rock in Deep Cove is short enough for a lunch break but the view over Indian Arm hits hard enough to ruin every office window forever.
adventure.bonus: Climb to the highest exposed rock face and sit with your legs dangling over the edge for a full 60 seconds.

adventure.title: Ski or Snowshoe at Mount Seymour
adventure.description: The most accessible of Vancouver's three ski mountains delivers real powder runs with zero alpine pretension and a local crowd that actually lives here.
adventure.bonus: Take the rope tow up to Goldie Lake and snowshoe the loop in the dark with only your phone light.

adventure.title: Swim at Wreck Beach
adventure.description: Canada's largest clothing-optional beach sits at the bottom of 500 UBC forest stairs and feels like a different country entirely.
adventure.bonus: Go full clothing-optional for at least one swim — you'll understand the vibe immediately.

adventure.title: Kayak Indian Arm from Deep Cove
adventure.description: Paddle into one of BC's most dramatic saltwater fjords straight from a sleepy North Van village where bald eagles are a common interruption.
adventure.bonus: Paddle all the way to Racoon Island and touch the rocks before turning back.

adventure.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard on English Bay
adventure.description: Balance your way across calm water with Stanley Park on one side and the city skyline on the other.
adventure.bonus: Try to stand the entire session without kneeling once.

adventure.title: Kayak False Creek at Sunset
adventure.description: Rent from Creekside Kayaks at Olympic Village and glide past yachts, seaplanes, and the glowing downtown skyline at golden hour.
adventure.bonus: Paddle all the way to the Olympic Village and back without a break.

adventure.title: Conquer the Grouse Grind
adventure.description: Grind up 2,830 punishing steps of 'Mother Nature's Stairmaster' and ride the Skyride down with a view you earned.
adventure.bonus: Do it without stopping to check your time on the app.

adventure.title: Ride the Stanley Park Seawall
adventure.description: Rent a bike at Spokes and cruise all 10km of the seawall's totem poles, beaches, and mountain views.
adventure.bonus: Stop for a photo at Siwash Rock without checking your phone once.

adventure.title: Zipline the Treetops at Grouse Mountain
adventure.description: Fly through five ziplines strung between old-growth trees, 100 feet above the mountain floor.
adventure.bonus: Let go of the brake line and go full speed on the longest run.

adventure.title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
adventure.description: Sway 70 meters above a rainforest canyon on one of the world's most famous suspension bridges, then wander the treetop walkways.
adventure.bonus: Walk the Cliffwalk section without holding the railing, if you're steady on your feet.

adventure.title: Whale Watching from Granville Island
adventure.description: Board a Prince of Whales zodiac from Granville Island and chase orcas and humpbacks through the Salish Sea.
adventure.bonus: Skip the top deck and watch your first sighting from the bow.

culture.title: Afternoon at the Vancouver Art Gallery
culture.description: The VAG's permanent Emily Carr collection — her towering Pacific forest canvases — is one of the most underrated art experiences in North America and hits differently every single time.
culture.bonus: Pick one Emily Carr painting, stand two feet from it for five minutes, and write down what you actually see.

culture.title: Afternoon at the Museum of Anthropology at UBC
culture.description: Arthur Erickson's glass-and-concrete masterpiece on the UBC cliffs houses the world's finest collection of Northwest Coast Indigenous art, including Bill Reid's monumental Raven and the First Men.
culture.bonus: Find a totem pole or sculpture that stops you completely — sit in front of it for ten full minutes without your phone.

culture.title: Read at the VPL Central Branch
culture.description: Moshe Safdie's soaring downtown library building opened in 1995 and remains one of the most quietly spectacular public spaces in any Canadian city.
culture.bonus: Pick a book from a shelf completely at random and read the first chapter before you leave.

culture.title: Catch a Canucks Game at Rogers Arena
culture.description: Feel downtown Vancouver shake as the Canucks take the ice in front of a sold-out, blue-and-green crowd.
culture.bonus: Learn one player's name and cheer for them specifically all night.

culture.title: Explore the Bill Reid Gallery
culture.description: Slow down inside a quiet downtown gallery devoted entirely to Northwest Coast Indigenous art.
culture.bonus: Spend five full minutes with one piece before moving on.

foodie.title: Craft Beer Flight at Brassneck Brewery
foodie.description: Brassneck's narrow Main Street taproom has been the heartbeat of Vancouver's craft beer scene since 2013, pouring weird, wonderful small-batch releases on a chalkboard that changes weekly.
foodie.bonus: Order the most aggressively named beer on the board without reading the description first.

foodie.title: Dinner at Ask for Luigi in Railtown
foodie.description: This tiny Railtown pasta bar has been impossibly hard to get into for a decade because the handmade orecchiette and gnudi are simply the best Italian food in the city.
foodie.bonus: Go without a reservation, put your name on the walk-in list, and spend the wait exploring Railtown.

foodie.title: Pastry and Espresso at Beaucoup Bakery
foodie.description: Jackie Kai Ellis's South Granville bakery produces Paris-caliber croissants and mille-feuille in a spare, beautiful room that makes a Tuesday morning feel like an occasion.
foodie.bonus: Buy a pastry for the next person who walks in behind you.

foodie.title: Lunch at La Taqueria Pinche Taco Shop
foodie.description: Vancouver's tightest, most authentic Mexican counter slings slow-braised birria and lengua tacos on handmade tortillas from a tiny Hastings Street space with zero pretension.
foodie.bonus: Order the lengua taco — if it grosses you out, you have to order a second one.

foodie.title: Cocktails at The Keefer Bar in Chinatown
foodie.description: The Keefer channels Chinatown's apothecary history into a moody, dark-wood bar where every cocktail is built around an herb, tincture, or botanical you won't find anywhere else in the city.
foodie.bonus: Let the bartender pick your drink — no input from you whatsoever.

foodie.title: Sushi Omakase at Tojo's Restaurant
foodie.description: Tojo Hidekazu, the chef credited with inventing the California roll, still presides over his eponymous West Broadway restaurant where omakase is a genuine conversation with a legend.
foodie.bonus: Ask Chef Tojo or your itamae what their single favorite piece is tonight and order it.

foodie.title: Brunch at Cafe Medina
foodie.description: This downtown institution's Belgian liege waffles and rose harissa shakshuka have anchored Vancouver weekend mornings for over fifteen years.
foodie.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever is queuing next to you before you get inside.

foodie.title: Oysters at Rodney's Oyster House
foodie.description: Vancouver's most beloved oyster bar serves a rotating selection of two dozen bivalve varieties shucked to order at a loud, joyful counter on Railway Street.
foodie.bonus: Order one variety you've never heard of and finish the shell liquor.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Sun Sui Wah on Main Street
foodie.description: Vancouver has some of the best Cantonese food outside Hong Kong and this Main Street classic — open since 1984 — is where you go to understand why locals mean it.
foodie.bonus: Order something from the cart you cannot identify by sight — no Googling before you eat it.

foodie.title: Ramen at Motomachi Shokudo
foodie.description: This tiny, cash-only Robson Street institution has been serving some of Vancouver's most precise tonkotsu for over two decades to queues that do not lie.
foodie.bonus: Order the spicy miso with an extra chashu and finish every drop of broth — no shortcuts.

foodie.title: Dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant
foodie.description: David Hawksworth's flagship in the Hotel Georgia is Vancouver's most enduring power dining room — the kind of room where the food actually justifies the occasion.
foodie.bonus: Order the tasting menu blind — tell the server your only two dislikes and let them handle everything else.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Crawl in Richmond
foodie.description: Hit two or three of Richmond's legendary dim sum houses back to back — some of the best outside Hong Kong.
foodie.bonus: Order one dish you can't identify and eat it anyway.

foodie.title: Browse Granville Island Public Market
foodie.description: Graze your way through fresh seafood, produce, and pastry stalls under one buzzing roof on the water.
foodie.bonus: Buy one thing from a vendor you've never tried.

foodie.title: Richmond Night Market
foodie.description: Wander North America's largest night market for stinky tofu, bubble waffles, and neon-lit stalls until midnight.
foodie.bonus: Try a street food you can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Coffee Crawl on Commercial Drive
foodie.description: Walk 'The Drive' and hop between indie cafes, Italian delis, and the neighborhood's best people-watching.
foodie.bonus: Order in Italian at one of the old-school espresso bars.
